name: Morgan Stahr, United for Democracy
subject: Why Trump wants to destroy this iconic American mural
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
If they can destroy Social Security’s history without a fight, they can destroy the whole program. | |
---
Peter, First, Trump bulldozed the East Wing of the White House. Then he announced the takeover and knocking down of the Kennedy Center. **Now, he’s quietly trying to destroy Social Security’s history:** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38LIZVpoph_6PbvN2SSyJbjLqmuFj01X5DNQMPuT76124EzTozlG1TOIFyKvb0Wibcgo29m8BuY4GZaYcnLhGfNLBgcWK1X0ZYyKuocE2tvyK5-ij0VveLcTJSEFah82fMqB6caAOvEKg1eE4qIKGzJ0NiZNFpdgIknEdeWB4WndXrGavMt77i2h94bDSG2dzga0sU2KbnUUjnaCExdKlH3M3-MMDHwdJGe2sA49Tr430iCMPCowjJ5I6xbgfNrIiEoe7z-nlYnoToL_wttJ0vqSWB1VjsCthW6ZfFa08sDFuqVYNxH5LbVTh0gM0I5lHBQQYA3n22wYnEWP__pp7ai50Nc2NoDClj0ACcEH9nVF15oNYFGS5d9ZulQBcAi_tSiQaHDn8jMgttKmR_OVqZS6583qwsFWLaIvewZclZwqepc_oY6Ij99SBnwnbdgBVzx0Q95tOs3Zv3qNx9pqg-e1VjPs0ko-WbVlHVtZCyX-HPEvGj6lexvjSCYcOpudJk/4o1/4sl3t3ICQUys8WRQ3TcUQQ/h0/h001.1RxDu4gpYDHYOZSfNkCKS0zUL7fI3CN34xAwDBW_YBs) Behind the doors of an unassuming federal building in Washington, D.C. lies an iconic New Deal-era mural depicting the promise of Social Security—walls and walls of publicly owned American art. The Trump administration is now considering selling the Wilbur J. Cohen building to a private developer, which means its inevitable destruction. **But this is about more than the beautiful frescoes and historic buildings. This administration believes it can take a bulldozer to Social Security itself, starting with its history.** Authoritarians and wannabe dictators reshape our society by chipping away at our values and our programs piece by piece. **If they can destroy Social Security’s historic murals without a fight, they can destroy the whole program.** [**We must fight back against Trump’s Orwellian plot to erase Social Security. Write to the General Services Administration and demand they halt all plans to demolish the Wilbur J. Cohen building immediately >>**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38LIZVpoph_6PbvN2SSyJbjLqmuFj01X5DNQMPuT76124EzTozlG1TOIFyKvb0Wibcgo29m8BuY4GZaYcnLhGfNLBgcWK1X0ZYyKuocE2tvyK5-ij0VveLcTJSEFah82fMqB6caAOvEKg1eE4qIKGzJ0NiZNFpdgIknEdeWB4WndXrGavMt77i2h94bDSG2dzga0sU2KbnUUjnaCExdKlH3M3-MMDHwdJGe2sA49Tr430iCMPCowjJ5I6xbgfNrIiE4Lj7nrdjYDwU2AeLDl4mVVf_xKFKXHTgFKs_0CwOGQm4_VFkVjKUkyffAkU4edm3GtdCwAgIkKRQm8-wwrldSfL9VNai-glfa_-WWMh6wJta16g-6tjV8dmsH5fwvqWz4lnwCuChzDsGh-WM2nE3UD9gQPs9QOEqniKxssoeCfbFcWUBxSlDxTD4Imnp2u9c2IDvEJUO77oIDo_j6WV8bCcNo-ZXnDElYuUPGOXj5eYB3GCBcjFaoEAySbVqRRJo/4o1/4sl3t3ICQUys8WRQ3TcUQQ/h1/h001.qnWS03gmi3qwvQowsWLtkzRD7kcB8I528J8gzmldk_4) The MAGA billionaires behind the packing of the Supreme Court are using the same levers of power to eradicate the importance and value of Social Security for the millions of people it's been promised to. **Just last week, CMS Administrator Dr. Oz claimed that Americans should work longer, and have shorter retirements, in order to boost the economy.** This type of propaganda is exactly how the powers that be chip away at our benefits and our democracy without a fight. Before Social Security was enacted, half of seniors lived in poverty. Today, fewer than 10% do. **This is what they want you to forget so they can demolish a vital American program—starting with erasing its New Deal-era art.** It’s up to us to stand up for our democracy and our American programs. [**Stand up for Social Security. Demand the Acting Administrator of the GSA save the Wilbur J. Cohen Federal Building.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38LIZVpoph_6PbvN2SSyJbjLqmuFj01X5DNQMPuT76124EzTozlG1TOIFyKvb0Wibcgo29m8BuY4GZaYcnLhGfNLBgcWK1X0ZYyKuocE2tvyK5-ij0VveLcTJSEFah82fMqB6caAOvEKg1eE4qIKGzJ0NiZNFpdgIknEdeWB4WndXrGavMt77i2h94bDSG2dzga0sU2KbnUUjnaCExdKlH3M3-MMDHwdJGe2sA49Tr430iCMPCowjJ5I6xbgfNrIiGrlmlSNkLRqKTnd0mSDNhyNrGMtQ84rR1gXfbJCNx1aRicW22Hy8Zv4tTfQ_h6xIi6V4KVUNb2zdW7TDjKV8bDu3f28v_RM1lchlN7A-LrB3SgVP9gG8QwZ1EjLufIuQsFs8CIXPWOkaP55VyLioFAtRyYPofUQ0vox6zbSeEKC7hSgIV-odm5HNIAic4BrunfuwMfQwqsiDa9sTMo5YePAfMJNOT2a0L3eP4lwlos8v_Jyp2WnpHmCBersQyZkuw/4o1/4sl3t3ICQUys8WRQ3TcUQQ/h2/h001.tqOwPEI0I2f3UmOgARTQvgKAMEkAB7KxgLZHjOSn5gg) Thank you for fighting to stop authoritarianism in its tracks, Morgan Stahr

subject: CONFIDENTIAL: 2026 GOP battlefield update
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the NRSC
body:
Take the official Senate Majority Survey—then help fund the counterattack. | Fellow American,

I’m sending this note because Senate Republicans are heading into 2026 with a dangerous false sense of security.

# Update from Tessa’s Campaign
# Fundraising, Endorsements, Team Updates
---
|
---
| |
**Hi Friend!**
We’ve got some exciting news!
Our campaign is running stronger than ever and we are gearing up to *officially* earn the Democratic Party’s endorsement and beat MAGA Jay Obernolte!
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Endorsements Update**

* **Democratic Party** : We have officially earned the “pre-endorsement” of the California Democratic Party, with over 93% of the delegate vote. That endorsement will be finalized at the CADEM Convention on 2/21, and we will have the Official Democratic Party Endorsement at that time!

* The three Democrats that were originally in this race with me are all supporting me now! My good friends **Alexis Claiborne** , **Paul Chakalian** , and**Edwin Alonso** , have all suspended their campaigns and are now joining forces with us to win this critical seat!

* Here’s a list of other endorsements we’ve earned recently:
* **Teamsters Local 1932**
* **Southern California Armenian Democrats**
* **San Bernardino County Young Democrats**
* **Democratic Club of Big Bear Valley**
* **Democrats of the Morongo Basin**
* **Redlands Area Democratic Club**
* Assemblymember**Dr. Corey Jackson**
* Assemblymember**John Harabedian**
* Moreno Valley Mayor **Ulises Cabrera**
* Big Bear Lake Mayor **Randall Putz**
* Riverside City Councilmember **Clarissa Cervantes**
* High Desert Progressive Democrats President **Seta Ghazarian**
* Immigrant Rights Organizer/Social Media Creator **Alan Vargas**
* DNC Member **Joe Salas**
* First Vice Chair for the San Bernardino County Democratic Central Committee **Sarah Gardam-Thomas**
* Los Angeles County Democratic Party AD 34 Chair **Denise Latanzi**

---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Team Update**

Recently, Alex Ortega was appointed **Campaign Manager** for our team! She previously worked on Derek Marshall for Congress and Chris Bubser for Congress.
Additionally, Jack Yao and his team at **SC Strategies** continues to be of huge help to our efforts. Jack and his team joined us back in the summer of 2025. Jack and SC Strategies has worked with Congresswomen Barbara Lee, Cori Bush, and Jill Tokuda, as well as California Assemblymembers Corey Jackson, Robert Garcia, and Tasha Boerner.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |

* * *

TPUSA's All-American Halftime Show

Turning Point USA's inaugural "All-American Halftime Show" crushed expectations, [pulling in over](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD3OpDAQRE8DmVGPzdgQONiEbDbdEPXYzdCSfxA2sMdfsdJc4Msqqad69ec1v5ADp89vjGTdybPPfsYQMNLODtOKYakcqaz5KnmWILUAKWCcU5hl663zWsmW7MMY0IMyZmxX-1zUSL13GrxWg1toVIORS_829AQ9mJbtTQL5AAClH7qD3uFTvjX03oByY9PDsXmsVDqXU6H9xMoncUr5Tjl1Lsc22LXWrTTqVyOnRk7XdXVL_pvoumuxkVMkz9jIqR574vQRW-ZUxVFQeHIBdyoCQxBfXfH1FbewiFgKnyTK4RyVIlyOkWsREqQRO93Qdrd-uzgELto0PXwicvg_rv7gz9PKfwEAAP__06iIHQ) 20 million views across social platforms—and climbing. The show, [featuring Kid Rock](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LGOpDAMBuCnCV1GxkBYihTX0O21V6JM4h0sJQ4iGXKPf-KkfYHtXPj_9ev787l9Oo4sr98ukfUXbyGHzcXoEp3snewuflVOVPbcSt4Q0GhADcsmccMuWB_MgB3Zfp7BfAzzvHS7NeGJ_rl8wYRhDGGEvu-p99M8Pefpw5uO7d0E2APAYHrzgNG7CZ8GxjDD4Bc1wvsIrlJ5-CyFzstVvohF8n1leficumj3Wo-ihl8KV4Vra-3RXNlZXjUL_XWJhc77VeEq1IrClaTSWR1LIqkK13GcYAFUuNb3KSwvfWSWqt_FaQSdOEbOoi-mRmfRLkb9jaO_dfTNo3DtThuOdieKmdUIr-Q4_l9af4B7WfwXAAD__zdki2s), Brantley Gilbert, Lee Brice, and Gabby Barrett, delivered patriotic performances that celebrated faith, family, and freedom, while the NFL showcased leftist rapper Bad Bunny. TPUSA announced [it will return](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0L2OpDAMB_CnCV1QcLgwFCmuoZtrr0Qm8Q6WQoKIB15_xUrzAttYLvzx1-__c34iJ86vf7iRDyfPscQZU8KNDg6YV0xfwhvVtVy1zGDAaQPajHNOMzTRh-gsNOS7YTDuYYdhbFYPzmIYsBtDj0BA2I1dF4Hc8ggjWtuwvy8Z6Iwx1nWuNX3AP7A408fB2DCq3rz3iEK1DSVXOk4UPolzLndXchvK1iS_iuxV2b8KJgXTdV3tchDLgofcEwomykKHIOeNsiiY7scKJgN3edxLKGHViU_S8j4y55feC2fR74pVY0r6g6E_GvrmUDA1h4_7xSlxdYPqzWtDTj_J5BeYp4fvAAAA___cZ4R2) in 2027 with another alternative show, predicting that final viewership could reach 40-50 million as numbers continue to climb. This is how you counter woke corporate entertainment—give Americans content worth celebrating. ★★★
Appeals Court Hands Trump Immigration Victory

An appeals court [delivered a major](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL1urTAQhJ8GOiNjuBgKF7ehO2lToj32Aiutf4QNJG8fkUdIN803M_o-X8sLiClsH-DR2IsWF90CzODxIAthB14Lecx7vHNclFSDkErIaQm8qNoZ64ZO1WhareUwdlpP9W6mEVdorVad7kZwGvoJXI8aejWifKuazNMkVSul7IZ2aGRv4Z96D7J3WnZ2qnp5JgcFc2NjyHhcUOhCCiE-KYbGRl-z2UtJuer-V2qu1Hzfd7PGr4D3g_lKzSkyFbK5UvOKDg9gASkhcBY2nkcRZ9ojuyzKcfokPOQsHBYMz4Z4aPstiBk3YEHe03ZAKLk-jEs3MVMedNXLzQPx76XyB4uXUT8BAAD__1JIhes) win for President Trump's border enforcement, blocking the release of migrants in a decision that strengthens the administration's ability to detain illegal immigrants. [The 5th Circuit](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLESnSAQRb8GO96sKw-1oEhj99KmdFbg6SYIDqD-fsZ8QpqdU-yce-f--swf4sBx_Um7N_bi2SU3Uwi0-8yW4kbhW3n3ZUt3STMCagkoYZxjmLFxxjrdYeNN2_egh67vx2Yz-j20NCzwfSulhi8AKfIWBmxH_wZcGjaPCbAFgE63-gXK0hsXDcr10NlRKDgPR9WXl02x-HxR5ctzjOmhFF827U0wW61HEd0PgZPA6b7v15I914VyfT4ETkcKXNkWgdOTKXACfM5DN0dZ87kfko7DUyjSpjNXuYRk_xT5-3SrLzL74KlwXOXOa6ZYH1eTjTtuDoGL7oWCdScO_0rV_9jxMvg3AAD__4jRgiI) ruled Friday that Trump's mass detention policy can continue, upholding the administration's authority to hold illegal aliens without bond hearings. House Republicans [called the Texas](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2ypCAUhJ9GM6YQvHANCDaZbDbd0GLgKKfm8FOAuo-_5T7CzTrpr7q_P6_1ZZEw7b9tBONOXH32qyWyESo6m4KlrWOEFvLV8iq4UIwLxpc10SpGb5xXUoxgJq25-pZaL2Mwy6w3P0k9f8-zBanctmgt319abmpZJjeiuUlcTJxzqSb14LOzX-Kt-Ow1l24ZZn4Ubzu0h8upQT1txxMwpXynnB4ux5FM6L20Qf4axHMQz-u6Hlv-m-C6a3EQz5IJO7o2iGeFcrzpPsUu-wF2FOYsEWsFHFpiQOBuMmshuw9UFnAPhHvoje25sH7UlI_OIvoONbKK7dPGany5kAib0sPM92iR_m_rP9B5GvEvAAD__0xaiII) special election loss a wake-up call to focus on the administration's most popular messages ahead of the critical midterm elections. ★★★
Iran Talks Move Forward Despite Tehran's Games

U.S. and Iranian officials held face-to-face nuclear talks in Oman over the weekend, the first such meetings since [U.S. strikes on Iran's nuclear sites](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDtuwzAQRE8jdRQo6kOrYJHGndOmFDbk0lqYH4FLSzl-oBwh3WCANxi8r8f6AAqUnp8Q0diDVpfdCiFAxEIW0gbBV4rIWz45r0qqWUgl5LKmsKrWGevmQbVoeq3lfBu0XtrNjJNbtO69RLhZvPW9m7RdtF9gcJMdsSVzLUnVSymHuZ87OVqY1PcsR6flYJdmlO_dQUXubE6M5YBKB1JK-Uo5dTbHNpit1p2b4aNR90bdz_PsfP5JeF5YvJpcgmvU_c1iz0wXyQKo2AK-CgulEBYWXAu9UOwBqs8lsojkXECBwFVQgSTS2waEIiqEFwveyFeRI6S2GLefFALxrJtRPiNQ-DtX_-HzMOo3AAD__7BjiXw) last June. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is "ready to fight so that no one dares to fight us," showcasing the regime's typical bluster. President Trump called the talks ["very good"](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0DGO3iAUBODT4I5f-MHC74IijbtNm9J6hrc2CgYLsEluHzlH2G6KT6PR_PpcPjHEkLafeJB1d1h89gvGiAeV4DDtGL9aOKjuude8gADNBXAxLSkuMHjrvJYwkB2NEfotjZmG3fqvUb0n6RzBuMqPyaxKS4caVjN69NMQ7NMkYBRCSD3ql1AOP2DVQnkjpJuYEtfpsVF9uZwqlRtbuCmklJ-U08vlY4h2b-2sTP5gMDOYe--vjnUPaWs50R88QqLyUAZzol4fs4dGfM9XJQazUmoy7zeDuZXrOHnD-LvyUDDxm8pfvuXseco8XS4SFt4Jz5wq94SRwTwU688eYgxVG6bEdmCI_6e1b7x5W_gXAAD__zmphfA) and demanded zero nuclear capability from Iran—the only acceptable outcome for American security and Middle East stability. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is [meeting with Trump](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2O2zAQhJ-G6mhQKx1pFSzSqLu0KYU1uTktjj8Cubbitw-UR0gzmGIw32B-fW6fyInL10_M5MOLt1jjhilhpsYBy47pt3Cmvtez1w0MWG1Am2UraYMh-hDtBAP50Tlj75Nzy7D72bnHFNF8TBbvMC73EZYYorUBJ-cIB_ZXk4HRGDPZ0d7MHPADHtbM0ZkpLGo2zyOiUL-FWjq1Fwq_iEupl6vlFmoekt9Fjq6mHwpWBet5nrdHI5YHNrkSCtajJhYOXcF6MRWsBi5xCtZCguWN-1NL1ZlItLRnPvRJsVCP-NZcOnfpmhsWLZi-u-YS0jOSztw7J-oaS9RHq3_eupCctX1frKH5eJycEnfr1Gy-MnL6N1r-4-eXh78BAAD__3Adjvk) this week to ensure any deal addresses Iran's ballistic missiles and regional terrorism. Maximum pressure works.

House Conservatives Hold the Line

With their [razor-thin majority](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD2ynDAQhE8DmahZCUsQKHBC9pw6pIQ0LPNWfyVpwXt7Fz6Cs0666-vv99f6ZchTfP4yAbU9aXXJrcZ7E7CQNfEwfm8UsB7pqmnlwCUDzmBeo19577R1UvAe9UMpkJNQau4PvTncZj6CdKDsbMWsuJtwB5wmIdS296TvJeAPABDyIQcYrfnBNwmjUyDs3I3wzs40rINNsWI5TaMTKcZ0pxQHm0Lv9dFarp342fGl48t1XcOe_kS87lro-JKTp0a2dnwpmN-bv0-xYL5TofZhheqL-ZReTLJnyqxiNA1ZRdMqC6k29o0pm-I-LJBrWAJDj_YGqIMJuS_a5Yu8pypVN8IzGPL_0Np_2Dw1_xsAAP__cSKIdA), House Republicans continue navigating the delicate balance between advancing President Trump's agenda and maintaining party unity as critical votes loom.

★★★
GOP Retreat Reveals Midterm Anxieties

Senate Republicans gathered in Palm Beach this weekend, where [NRSC Chair Tim Scott delivered sobering polling](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2unjAMhq8GNpAJ-ZKTIUMXttO1IzKJ-bCUH0RySC-_oqp6AWez7MevXj2_PtdP5MDp_RMjWXfz6rNfMQSMdLHDdGDYK0cqR24lrwKEGkAMYNYUVtF767yaRU920hrUx6y16Q_rt915Y1ARoQajld5hkx-4TXJ_mRl6tk8SiAkAZjWpEaTDl9gUSK9hdqaT8HV6rFRGl1Oh68bKN3FK-ZlyGl2OfbBHrWfp5h-dWDqxtNbGhuXg9K450W-MnOh60E4siVp5mP_3oZC7qD5LKV-gzdyJpVDCSsNF59cWHgPlHzY0wjOnIbKvdMXhIPSNk3_e-8v6s3EIXJTuJLwjcvjbsH5D6m3FnwAAAP__wNaJlg) showing Democrats' 6-point generic ballot lead could threaten seats in Maine and Texas, tempering optimism despite MAGA Inc.'s $300 million war chest.

★★★
Democrats Riding Special Election Wave

Democrats continued their 2025 upset streak, with [a Louisiana special election victory](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD2O5CAQRk-DM1rlgoHpgGATZ7PphlYNVLdL4scydHuPv_IeYbIXfPr09P58rV8kWerzNxUO8S1rammlnKnwIZHqRvkxpHDf2tnbioBOA2q4rzWvOKUQkzM4cZi9B_dpvL9PW2APYL7R4KfBB7HF2c_xbqxHxnlOPEm4ngBnADBudjewkT7w24FNHky8KwuvPdHgfoutdj7eNOTNUmu7qNVbbGXKYRtj78r8UrgoXM7zvJ3UN6nP0Sr_pSKVj2uqcKl8doVLpLKTPOvFfdBghYu1H2CdUbgkLi0eNLp-7Z2HHser7DpJH4fE0XVuL-lClXTfOQplzZnjJaRwmY6Q9lNylu68svAsJPm_6PhB23fAfwEAAP__CUSK4g) adding to major swings in Texas and Iowa. The pattern has Republicans worried about November turnout as Democrats outperform in Trump districts.

* * *

Kiley Pushes Biolab Legislation
Rep. Kevin Kiley (R-CA) is [urging Congress](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLFuhDAQRL_GdKBlMfZd4SKNu0ubEi22OVZn7NOZmOTvI6J8QZrRjEYaPc3HbboRR073d9qCcZUnn_1EMdIWXuworRSXnbdQ1nyUPCGgagFbuE4pTth447wasAmm1xrUZdD62qxmDPMIM4ACxFmPIKVfelpo0eCUHGTD5lwC7AFgUL3qQDoacVYgvYbBXYWEz6enPZTO5VTCq9LONXBK-XQ5dS5vTTTrvj-LGN4EWoH2OI4uhaNs9HX2Au1favcq0D5C5dQ-OIbvduYcaW4jlbbeAxWB9kQSaAFP0QIte4G2RzniZRRom5fxz4Nj5KK0kHDfiOMvx_6P66rBnwAAAP__Utd6ag) to pass the Preventing Illegal Laboratories and Protecting Public Health Act following the FBI's discovery of an illegal biolab in Las Vegas linked to Chinese Communist Party-connected operations in California. ★★★
Congress Faces DHS Funding Deadline

Lawmakers are debating Department of Homeland Security funding as [another deadline](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0D1ywyAQxfHToM6a1YL4KCjSqHPalBoMa2tnEHgsInL8jHOEdK95v-L_dV2vgTOXx2fYyceT11TTGnIOO704hrKFfG-807HVftQVAfUF8AJuLXnFIfmYtMSB_GQMaCuNccPmKcwgHaobKesmaZHIRWVn0tJEY-XA_i0BTgAg9aRHUDHMeNOgkgEZnVDw_Uyh0THGWg56naHxSVxKfa9axlj3Ifuttech5IfAReDSex_v9adQf992gcvJiarARUtr3WxxxmnC4eXTs3POfGgjFDz2wPkPbP9ocHr8DQAA__-1UGjE) looms. Democrats are pushing to restrict ICE operations after recent unrest in Minneapolis, while Republicans seek to maintain current enforcement priorities

★★★
New York Legalizes Assisted Suicide

Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation making New York the 13th state to [legalize physician-assisted suicide](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOpDAQRL_GZEZNw5khcHAJ2Vx6IWrsZmitsRH2gHa_fsV-wialCkpVpff_OT1JgsTXP9rYulMmn_xEIdDGhziKK4WlyMZ5TVdOEwIaDahhmGKYsPLWedNixbbpezCPtu-HarU0k186NzfEZu7axSyPwbsGHqZ3ZFxTib2bABsAaE1jaugc_cHZQOd7aN2gOnjvngrn2qWY-TipyMkSY7pdirVLWxXsWsqeVftX4ahwvK6rng-WMtNR7oTCcU9BiriscLw3FY6AtwwKx8iX_kzHh57ZpY2zbtqy6lyosC5JB35RkC_WlLPkwl7ntzjxrHCsDuv3S0KQbHrVwWsjCT-nyi84nha_AwAA___A8IK1) for terminally ill patients with less than six months to live. Cardinal Timothy Dolan condemned the law as promoting a "Culture of Death."

subject: I declined
body:
As a former CIA officer, I’ve seen democracies flicker out.
---
Derek — In November, myself and five other members of Congress made a video quoting current law, that the military has a responsibility to refuse illegal orders. In response, President Trump tweeted more than a dozen times, calling for me to be investigated, arrested, and hanged. Since then, the FBI and former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, now U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me for the inquiry. I wanted to share an important update on all of this, and ask for your help. I wrote to Attorney General Pam Bondi and U.S. Attorney Pirro to inform them that I won’t be doing an interview, and that their offices should preserve their records should I decide to sue for their infringement on my constitutional rights. I am not going to legitimize what they’re doing. The video in question was public, and I’ve talked about it extensively in the open. Our Constitution is crystal clear about our freedom of speech, and that’s a value worth fighting for. To be honest, very smart people have told me to keep my head down and be quiet — that doing so would make this inquiry go away. But that’s exactly what Trump and Pirro want. They are employing intimidation to get me to shut up and, much more importantly, to deter other people from criticizing them. So I’m taking the opposite approach, and I am fighting back, because this is bigger than any one senator or any one video. If they can do this to me, what can they do to a business leader, or the head of a community foundation, or a mom who goes viral on the internet for criticizing Donald Trump? We all own our choices. I own mine. And Pirro and Trump must own theirs. This is where I need your help. As I’ve said before, fighting back against these abuses of power requires a political strategy and a legal strategy. We’re opening up an entire new front on the legal strategy — one that goes on offense. But taken together, it requires resources, and that is why I am asking: [**Can you please split a contribution between my campaign and the DNC to continue fighting back against a president hell-bent on revenge against those who speak out?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-slotkin-split?refcode=em_20260209_6029_fr&amount=20&refcode2=6029_22930333_Rc1B4j&akid=6029%2E22930333%2ERc1B4j)

body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
@ariberman.bsky.social: SCOTUS decision killing what’s left of Voting Rights Act could cost Dems 19 House seats, eliminate every majority-minority district in South, eviscerate 14th/15th Amendments & fulfill John Roberts 40-year crusade against country’s most important civil rights law [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=020926_3&amount=25]
The impact shows how partisan this all is, Team. A complete dismantling of the Voting Rights Act -- a key civil rights law -- would only harm one political party and return parts of the country to a suppressive era we left behind sixty years ago.
During the oral arguments in Louisiana v. Callais , at least five conservative justices seemed ready to handicap the VRA so that it will no longer stop white majorities from locking racial minorities out of elected office through racial gerrymandering.
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. # NEWSLETTER FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,
**Week four** of the 2026 Legislative Session has come to a close in Tallahassee. I continue working alongside my colleagues to advance legislation that puts Florida first, with a focus on protecting freedoms, supporting families, and strengthening Florida’s future. I look forward to sharing updates as the session continues.
As always, please do not hesitate to [**contact my office**](https://us.list-manage.com/APzJs__hxzZ?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac) if there is something we can do for you. My team and I would be more than happy to help you in any way we can.
---
| |
# Bills Presented:
---
|
---
| |
* PCS for [**HB 529**](https://us.list-manage.com/89PRg1ut1ox?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac): Community-Based Lead Agency and Subcontractor Liability, which passed favorably in its first committee, **Civil Justice & Claims Subcommittee.**

* My Bill [**HB 221**](https://us.list-manage.com/EEm7LTe8uUo?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac) has passed its second committee and will allow an employee to waive the right to minimum wage if he or she was receiving other value in an internship, pre-apprenticeship, or on-the-job workforce training that could enhance their long-term, income-earning future. The concept of the bill... We live in a society where it has become the norm to spend $25k, $50k, or even $100k per year in college tuition to learn skills and earn a degree with the hope of a higher-paying job at the end of the journey. Many careers, however, do not require a degree, and many of these careers can often lead to even higher incomes because of the skills learned and value delivered. An unintended consequence of Florida’s Constitutional minimum wage is that it cripples an employer’s ability to provide more opportunities for unskilled workers in the areas of pre-apprenticeship and education. This bill fixes this. **If you want to watch the full debate on the Florida Channel link click here:**[**2/3/26 House Civil Justice & Claims Subcommittee - The Florida Channel **](https://us.list-manage.com/j0ENeAGXYPK?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac)

[**If you'd like to follow my bills, please click: Representative Ryan Chamberlin 2026- Sponsored Bills | Florida House of Representatives**](https://us.list-manage.com/VW9CIlbj7aK?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac)

Dear Peter, My friend Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren is an unsung hero for defending our democracy and our Constitution. I had not known Zoe well before our work together on the House Select Committee to investigate the January 6th attack on the United States Capitol, but I was aware of her reputation as one of the most effective and respected Members of the House of Representatives. She is a thoughtful and serious member, and she operates with zero ego — a rarity in Congress. Zoe has been a source of wisdom and good judgment for me and many Members in Congress. Although we don’t share many views on politics or public policy, I can assure you that we need Zoe in Congress and on the frontlines, especially in this moment when our democracy continues to be threatened. We all must look beyond party and support people like Zoe who will defend the Constitution, someone we know will do the right thing. subject: Gun Ban Moves Forward in New Mexico
body:
Plus: The $2.3M fraud story not a single mainstream outlet will touch | New for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=546939d4b8&e=567664f14c)
| | | | | |
Three bills. Three failures. One legislature completely out of control.
[New Mexico's Senate just passed a gun ban that even their own Democrats are calling unconstitutional.](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=194810d3af&e=567664f14c) Meanwhile, a story broke this week that should be leading every newscast in America — and not a single mainstream outlet will touch it.
---
[|
---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=1f3fde76c6&e=567664f14c)
| |
🔫 **NM SENATE PASSES GUN BAN — THEIR OWN PARTY SAYS IT'S UNCONSTITUTIONAL**
SB 17 cleared the Senate. It limits magazines to 10 rounds and bans the most popular sporting rifles in the state. Democratic Sen. Joe Cervantes voted against it. His reason? Listen to what he says on camera.
Then Krysty shares something personal — the stalker that forced her to get licensed to carry, and the night she locked herself in a closet with her kids with nothing but her firearm.
When you hear that story next to what these legislators just voted for, something clicks.

🏛️ **THE GOVERNOR RELEASES A VIDEO BEGGING HER OWN PARTY**
This is where it gets wild.
The healthcare crisis is so bad that the governor went on camera asking New Mexicans to call her own Democratic legislators and force them to act.
She lit this fire. Now it's burning out of control. Doctors are leaving. Rural hospitals are closing. And the bill that was supposed to fix it? It's being gutted by trial lawyers who sit on the legislature. Mark explains why this probably ends in a special session — and why even that might not work.

💡 **MIMI STEWART'S ENERGY BILL COULD GUT SCHOOL FUNDING AND MEDICAID**
SB 18 copies California's anti-energy playbook. The legislature's own nonpartisan financial report says it could crater the budget. We play the ad that's running against it right now. Germany and the UK already tried this. We show you what happened.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=d2d219e309&e=567664f14c)
---
| |
🚨 **$2.3 MILLION FRAUD RING — THE STORY THE MEDIA WON'T COVER**
A former mayor in Oregon uncovered something massive. A Venezuelan gang member. A woman kidnapped. What they did to her hands with a power tool — we can barely describe it.
She was left for dead.
The address connected to the crime? A fake rehab center pulling $2.3M in state Medicaid funds. It gets worse. That operation connects to a $60 million fraud ring laundering money to a country you would never guess. One journalist is covering this. One. We break down why.

🗳️ **83% OF AMERICANS AGREE ON VOTER ID — ONE SENATOR'S EXCUSE IS UNREAL**
Jamie Raskin went on CNN and said voter ID could hurt women. Krysty's response is the highlight of the episode. Then Fetterman shows up — in his hoodie — and says what 83% of the country is thinking. Plus: new population data showing a potential 14-seat House shift that explains everything.

⛷️ **LINDSEY VONN'S FINAL OLYMPICS**
She tore her ACL a week ago. She went anyway. At 41.
What happened at the third gate will stay with you. Mark's reaction says it all.
---

body:
Kristi Noem and her DHS’ brutality cannot go unanswered.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260209-5900-footer&t=1&akid=5900%2E420207%2Ew8Sz9g)
Peter,
Over the past several weeks, communities across the country have been shaken by the abusive tactics and deadly force employed by ICE agents. But this chaos didn’t happen in a vacuum. It’s a reflection of failed leadership, lack of oversight, and a refusal to take accountability at the highest level.
**Kristi Noem _is_ that failed leadership. **
She has defended the lawlessness and brutality of ICE and CBP, lied to our faces directly after the murders of Renee Good and Alex Pretti, and repeatedly refused to answer for any of the grave abuses ICE agents have committed under her watch.
When the safety of our neighbors is in jeopardy and rogue federal agencies are allowed to carry out violence with impunity, we have an obligation to take action.
As I said in _The Seattle Times_ :
> _“First we have to haul everybody, all of the leaders of these agencies that have been flouting the law, we have got to haul them before us ... we should impeach them... And we should make them answer to the American people.”_
Enough is enough _._ There are too many lives at stake, and we cannot allow this terror to become the new normal.
**That’s why I’m calling for the impeachment of Kristi Noem.**
[**Please join me in adding your name to this petition calling for her impeachment.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/impeach-kristi-noem/?sourcecode=em20260209-5900&t=2&akid=5900%2E420207%2Ew8Sz9g)
**[Add your name](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/impeach-kristi-noem/?sourcecode=em20260209-5900&t=3&akid=5900%2E420207%2Ew8Sz9g)**
Kristi Noem and her DHS have committed unforgivable abuses of power, and profoundly betrayed our trust. It’s time for her to go — **right now.**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

| | | | | | Hi, Peter,**520.6 campaign miles traveled this week!** Where did I go? Here are the highlights:******On Saturday,** The Denver Dems Central Committee Meeting on January 30th set the stage for our upcoming election season. I took the floor for candidate remarks and watched the discussion that will shape our 2026 process.
**On Sunday,** I attended the Silicon FlatIrons AI Panel, where I spoke about growing asymmetries in communication technology, and the ways in which AI is impacting our world, public policy, and civil rights negatively.
**On Monday,** I spoke on a bill that will allow people to sue immigration officers for alleged constitutional violations - a direct response to the horrific government use of force we are seeing in Minneapolis. I will do everything in my power this session to pass Senate Bill 26-5 to protect Coloradans.
**On Tuesday,** I attended the Fire Service Legislative Reception - as a former volunteer firefighter, I understand the risks and sacrifices of public service, and as State Treasurer, I’ll make sure those who protect us are protected in retirement.
**On Wednesday** , I introduced HB 26-1137, a law requiring transparency for Campaign Consultants, to ensure fair elections in our state, a move to protect our democracy.
**On Thursday** , a fabulous supporter hosted a house party to keep our campaign running - I don’t take corporate dollars, and they hate that because it means I can’t be controlled - these parties are so important to give us the funds we need to run this campaign. Our Special Guests, Maya Blasingame (2025 Civil Rights Awardee) and Muni Tox (Miss Trans Colorado ‘23-’24) spoke eloquently about why this race is so important in so many ways. It was a fun and uplifting night that reiterated why I do the work I do every day. Do you want to host a house party for us? [Reach out to my staff! ](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=1430d4215f&e=8249791cac)They will walk you through everything. **On Saturday** , I drove to and from Gunnison to attend the Gunnison County Democratic Winter Dinner. It’s important to me to show up at events throughout the state - when elected statewide, I will always strive to represent the interests of ALL Coloradans, not just those with proximity.
**Upcoming Events**
It will be another big week as we gear up to Caucus and Assembly in March. If you haven’t yet checked your [voter registration](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=46e4eea6b1&e=8249791cac), TODAY IS THE LAST DAY where you can make changes and still be eligible to caucus. You can find information on where your county is hosting Caucus and Assembly between March 3-7th here: [https://www.coloradodems.org/caucus/schedule ](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=98479c39e0&e=8249791cac)
I hope you plan to attend your Caucus and Assembly and that you’ll pledge to support me - help us track our commitments and show support in numbers by filling out this short Commit to Caucus pledge [https://www.briannaforco.com/caucus](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=20cee8c3d5&e=8249791cac)
For my day job, it’s a busy legislative week, but I’ll find time to hit the campaign trail and celebrate Valentine’s Day with my wife.
Later this week, I will be attending the Colorado Concern Legislative Reception to hear from legislators, cabinet leaders, and members of Colorado Concern for an informal and substantive conversation about Colorado’s most pressing issues. I will also be at the State of the State of Colorado’s film and video industry conference. As an avid champion of the arts, and the film industry, I want to be sure I am always in the know for the ways in which I can continue to support this critical industry, the jobs it can create, and the culture we can continue to support through film and video.
**Why Your Support Matters Right Now** 🚨 **Caucus & Assembly are coming — and this is where it all starts.** 🚨Caucus is one of the most important moments in our democracy, and every year turnout is way too low. That means the people who _do_ show up get an outsized say in where our party goes next. Showing up to caucus is the difference between feeling “meh” about the Democrats on your June primary ballot... and being genuinely excited to vote blue in November.Here’s the real talk: **if we don’t show up strong at Caucus and Assembly, our campaign ends there.** We’re building momentum and commitments every day, but our goal isn’t just to attend...it’s to be loud, organized, and visible.Caucus is active participation - you dedicate an evening to democracy! You show up. You meet your neighbors. You help decide the future of the party. And honestly? That’s what campaigns should be about. Building community, not just collecting votes.🗳️ **Commit to caucus and assembly March 3–7
** 👉 Pledge here:[ https://www.briannaforco.com/caucus](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=ecdb64bf8a&e=8249791cac)In just a couple hours on one night, **you can have a massive impact on our democracy.** Don’t wait until the primary! This is where your voice actually counts.

Here are the highlights:****On Saturday, The Denver Dems Central Committee Meeting on January 30th set the stage for our upcoming election season. I took the floor for candidate remarks and watched the discussion that will shape our 2026 process. On Sunday, I attended the Silicon FlatIrons AI Panel, where I spoke about growing asymmetries in communication technology, and the ways in which AI is impacting our world, public policy, and civil rights negatively. On Monday, I spoke on a bill that will allow people to sue immigration officers for alleged constitutional violations - a direct response to the horrific government use of force we are seeing in Minneapolis. I will do everything in my power this session to pass Senate Bill 26-5 to protect Coloradans. On Tuesday, I attended the Fire Service Legislative Reception - as a former volunteer firefighter, I understand the risks and sacrifices of public service, and as State Treasurer, I’ll make sure those who protect us are protected in retirement. On Wednesday , I introduced HB 26-1137, a law requiring transparency for Campaign Consultants, to ensure fair elections in our state, a move to protect our democracy. On Thursday , a fabulous supporter hosted a house party to keep our campaign running - I don’t take corporate dollars, and they hate that because it means I can’t be controlled - these parties are so important to give us the funds we need to run this campaign. Our Special Guests, Maya Blasingame (2025 Civil Rights Awardee) and Muni Tox (Miss Trans Colorado ‘23-’24) spoke eloquently about why this race is so important in so many ways. It was a fun and uplifting night that reiterated why I do the work I do every day. Do you want to host a house party for us? will walk you through everything. On Saturday , I drove to and from Gunnison to attend the Gunnison County Democratic Winter Dinner. It’s important to me to show up at events throughout the state - when elected statewide, I will always strive to represent the interests of ALL Coloradans, not just those with proximity. Folks - Michele Tafoya here! I never really considered running for office. Ever.

[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z1jf92uqkb90chvp10uqh38mcl3snu61p8s6use8_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) Folks - Michele Tafoya here! ** ** I never really considered running for office. Ever. I was too focused on raising my family, and being the best football sideline reporter I could be. ** ** But even in the last few weeks, Minnesota has become the embodiment of everything wrong with politics today. Tim Walz, his inner circle, and the corrupt political class are too busy: ** **
* Wasting billions of our tax dollars on fraudulent daycares
* Failing to condemn the activists storming churches
* Raising prices on hardworking families
* Sabotaging anything the President wants to do
* Forcing men into women's spaces
* Pitting Americans against each other

** ** I can't sit on the sidelines anymore. That's why I'm throwing my hat in the ring and announcing my candidacy for U.S. Senate! [Is there ANYTHING I can say to convince you to become one of my first donors? The far is already racing to destroy my campaign before it even gets off the ground. I can't shock the political world and flip this seat without your help.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zfh359udfip4hh2r2ges7qga449b0u5qql6v4pg0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) [ BECOME A FOUNDING DONOR ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zdb9gktv315ovf856t3ccveqsgvc5oecc6vf95o0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) I've thought long and hard about the dynamics of this race before jumping in. ** ** Minnesota has long been considered simply out of reach for Republicans. The last time it voted for a GOP President was Nixon. The pundits and political experts say a Republican could never win here. ** ** But this year is going to be different for three key reasons: ** ** FIRST - I'm running against Tim Walz's right hand. All the rampant fraud that took place here happened under Peggy Flanagan's nose as much as it did under his. We will remind voters about that fact every single day. ** ** SECOND - The President has increased his voter share each time he has run. He nearly flipped this state in the last election, and Kamala Harris' running mate was our sitting Governor! Momentum is on our side. ** ** THIRD - I'm a different kind of candidate, and I know how to win. I didn't reach the top of my industry by pulling my punches. I put in the work. I never backed down. And I kept fighting, no matter what the naysayers said. ** ** In my years on the sidelines, I've seen a LOT of underdogs win football games that the "experts" said were impossible. ** ** The Minnesota Senate race will be another chapter in that storied history. [But only with your help. Will you be one of the first-ever donors to my new campaign? This is going to be one of the MOST IMPORTANT races in the entire country. Your support - especially in these early days - will make the difference between victory and defeat.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z9tdd0s5cvo7u1s8j0voad8pc41qs0arl55iv32o_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) | [ PLEASE ADD $10 ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z6sih6mktn2pp3o0jros29rg22f0dgall97g887g_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) [ PLEASE ADD $50 ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z79mp1f2jv2roqnk0aj1vcg31d8bolj8sia2fl88_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) [ PLEASE ADD $250 ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zhkp5ucq2tdpnj6uoif0ec59mcu2ac7oc8lsd7mo_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) | [ PLEASE ADD $25 ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zm4pfnnrtivf8b65ibffkp75oa14el149tn8sp0o_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) [ PLEASE ADD $100 ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z1hrkc1ujms2ejhaj1pedum8755hvqf6jbmpo85o_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs) [ ANOTHER AMOUNT ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z87aolu7u2v35v6odq6fvipc26jhujb3fqn3iee0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0cth62o72c3h2bs)

## Netanyahu to Meet Trump Wednesday
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet President Trump in Washington on [Wednesday to discuss](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO8yAQhJ8Gd7aWNcFJQfE37vK3V1pglpgLhghvYuXtT05xL3DNNCN9o2--rtPVxhTz7b9dyXAoU6Z9S8RMdcrENr_t8uSyEjHX5_pwlex9QkDdArYSJm9jek-q8SYQIfUNGTkMMKDUZ9ksRlrl3Cy9sl753oPVJ6Wlg3DSOuhLaKI5aIASpIQzQCdPrgen_CXooHHWQgH5yKV23yVmXiikd3lR7eayNskszI9N9P8EjgLHfd-7Obv5KAWOB1rgCHjEIHD8dWo_Om2sNrds033rFl5TU41_7DGluOlBKLitNqbPEP_pnZfBnwAAAP__6o54TQ) ongoing negotiations with Iran, moving up his visit by a week from the originally planned Feb. 18 meeting. Netanyahu requested the [earlier meeting last Friday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGurCAQBuCnwQ4DI4JbUNzGbm97SwMyrNyDssHZNb79iZvzBqedSf4_3__vPt1dyml7_HUrWopl2vDYMxJhnTYkt51ueVFZEYnqa336iu5rAgGaC-BSTMGlfE6qCTYiAnYNWmmMMCD1IJvF3pTrewwaO98PszQmquBVF2Zvopujb5K90gRIIaUYhGhl7zvhVbhFHTXMmimBIVGp7f-SNlow5rO8sbZzWZtsF6Lnzro_DEYG43Ec7emWUq4vg_HiMBhdpTRn3D-XHxXfkfgF4x8ZPzBsuAd3cnnrB1C6F-1Ca26qDc8j5Zx2bZgSj9Wl_CmnXy32tvAdAAD__09mgYM), a day after Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks in Oman with Iran's foreign minister over a potential nuclear deal. Netanyahu's office said the prime minister believes any deal must include limits on Iran's ballistic missiles and ending support for militant groups, including Hezbollah and Hamas. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that if the U.S. attacks Iran, his country would [retaliate against U.S. bases](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO2zAMgOGnkTcFFKNTfIOGLN6uHQpcR0OxaJutLAUyfYbfvnDaN-hKAj_48edH_xE4cZ6-hYW8jKXPtK-JRKj2mSTkI8yblIVIpG7L81Ep_O4R0GlAbaCPgdPR2yb6kQjp2pA3txvc0LjWNLN3AYeAw2AA4T2ia2F09OZsawlsHNqG_VkDNGAMtAAX8_a4wsPG99GNDgenLFBkKfXyq3CWmcZ0lC-ql6EsTfKzyHNV17vCTmG37_tlWfO5U9hR1tuqsDtRCrtnSSw8_J38s2kpei4p6q1OlEWfUs6T3llm_SLrnWKmNYZDh4Wj5hqyzjQV4SBc8pkLVd_v5vPH53fbVB-fO6fEq7spC9MSOL1ulf968JfHPwEAAP__zF6SNA) in the region.
## Homeowners Hanging on Longer
Americans who sold homes in late 2025 had [owned them for an average of 8.55 years](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdKD1wpm7wkUaukubEhm8PpwYG9nLIf4-Ir-QdjQzmnlfz_FpfPDx9WlW0uzSGOkogZgpj5HYxNMsO6eViDnv6zZlMj8jAqoasJYwWuPDOXaV1Y4Iqa1Iy76HHqW6y2rR2Dslb9A6089wb11nbWfnh2tvEyE6VXl9tQFKkBLuAI28TS1MnX045RTOSnRA1nPKzXfykRdy4Uxvys2c1irohXkrov0QOAgcjuNorgvRsE8xpuNyCRymvfhIpQgczrTnek2RToHDklZKR6Rc6sLm9PFVbzvXczKFTbg0pitUZW23w4fgi-pFB6_V-PC3gP-F7a3xNwAA__8s74TE), the longest stretch in at least 25 years, according to new real estate data analysis. The trend is driven by a "lock-in effect" as homeowners hold onto ultra-low pandemic-era mortgage rates, with tight inventory and high prices making moves costlier. Coastal states [face the longest tenures](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkcGOnDAMQL8Gbh4lhoWZA4e5IFXV9lS1RxSIgbQhnsZmEX9fUe0f9Gi95ydZ_vk-vLsQQ1q-uY06nXlIdEgkVcpDInXpdOuuvBGp5n17jZnc7wENNmAQrBm8C_Ec6tJ3MxFSVVJn29a0aJu7LdeuQtuO_g3HGh-VrYhmV92bB1bovR3ruQzdVTNojbXmbszNvo2VGWv_mJu5wakpakM-KOfbLw5JV5rjyR-UbxNvZexW1ZcU1bPAvsD-OI7bJuliBfaUYJcCe-EpkJ4w7VH3TOCShzWIcj4_qYsQRHa67JU34iNRFggJdCUhmNiJugiiTknAZYKVow9pAU7KlxUyXJsCM-drhshpIdHPCCSngVOBvcvwfNofX7_8-V7mzr-OEGOQpi1qs2wuxH-H6X9946PDvwEAAP__nXijOA): Massachusetts leads at 13.29 years, followed by Connecticut at 13.02 years and California at 11.24 years. Maine had the shortest tenure at just 4.8 years, nearly 8.5 years less than Massachusetts. The lock-in effect may be easing, as more homeowners now carry mortgage rates above 6% rather than below 3%, potentially encouraging future sales.
## Olympics Scramble to Fix Medals Problem
Organizers of the Milan Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics say they are investigating after several athletes reported [problems with their medals](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OqzAQQOGnMV3QeCAmLlzchi633RL5ZxycNRiZSRBvv8q-wtZH-orzdZ_uNuW0Pv7bhQzHMq107JmYqU4rsV1PO7-4LETM9bVsrpL9nhBQXQAvEqZgUz6nvgkmEiF1DRk5DDCgVDfZzEZLDXKQgwzB9o66qB16FbQjsBiDbZL5aIASpIQbQCuvrgPXBx1VVOiV6IFC4lLbZ0krzxTzWd5UW1-WJpuZedtF90_gKHA8jqN1zn-awHHfSmWBo62cfKZd4Oj7xzU_r7pWXZpqwnaknNOuBtHDY7Ep_7L8pxdvgz8BAAD__3Dtczw) shortly after being awarded. U.S. alpine skier Breezy Johnson, who won gold in the women’s downhill, showed reporters that the ribbon had come apart from her medal during a post-race news conference, and several other winners [noted similar issues](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1yqzAQQOGnEZ2Z1QKSXai4MzekclLlp2MWWIwSCTFibcZvn3FeIf2Zrzgf5-5MPvjl8kKRnUypW3jfAotw7hYWWu40XyVFZpF8jWufmb47BDQHwIOGbiQf7l1djG5iRq4KdtpasKjNURezw2roocHe1lDriRhPbC0MdCI02IxN4d1DA9SgNRwBSt30FfT1eJrMZHAwqgYevaRcfiW_yMxTuKcb53JIsQhuFlk3Vf1T2Cps930v_bIJXTLFR6GwXRW2_9_mzzi_-qf3Z4Vtkd247j4EvxmrarhE8uHXkz9NuDn8CQAA__-hr2-7). The organizers of the Milan-Cortina 2026 games said they are giving the issue “maximum attention” and [working to identify the cause](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE8DnZF_WJstXKSh27Qp0QMeizf-QfbbReT0EavcIN1IMxrNN1-34QbOu3j_hICWljRE3ItHIsxDRIJ4wPqkFBCJ8jNsY0b4HiSXmnHJBB9mcP4Y2nq2C6JEVaMVxnAjhe5EvVpptDFqMtyorgNo26sywuh5VCN04oq1s2cbl4ILwTvOG3EZFR_b-broRctJVy3H2VHKzSO5SCsu_kgvzM2UQu3tSrSVSn1Usq9kv-97E8fppDj9SvZlS5lKJfvkj7C56ZRjRvw52COtsaTIwB8FmHdP9pdhQKtHwsICzuALe2OzPEWQl04oU2c7b7vz3hVtqpbfAzj_HkT_evFl5W8AAAD__6Y2iGM). Concerns about medal quality are not new. After the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris, more than 200 athletes requested replacements due to tarnishing or wear.

Homeowners Hanging on Longer Americans who sold homes in late 2025 had , the longest stretch in at least 25 years, according to new real estate data analysis. The trend is driven by a "lock-in effect" as homeowners hold onto ultra-low pandemic-era mortgage rates, with tight inventory and high prices making moves costlier. Coastal states : Massachusetts leads at 13.29 years, followed by Connecticut at 13.02 years and California at 11.24 years. Maine had the shortest tenure at just 4.8 years, nearly 8.5 years less than Massachusetts. The lock-in effect may be easing, as more homeowners now carry mortgage rates above 6% rather than below 3%, potentially encouraging future sales. Jasmine Crockett are leading their respective [Senate primary races](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOtB6IQEKF39Dl7-9Ei3xEqxbbGSvQnj7E_cK14000sx88_WYHuTFh9d_2tjqZ4lT4CMLq3KaMgdS3pPfKJ17FNG4v0k4TAh4rwArA5MjL-fUls7O4AZTsjVdBx22fT-Uq53vA3XOdXMPCL0DYh4AYYGmd-4230pvrzBAAwbBYFsTN8vQIjf0vC2m7YoW2HmNqdaVlT-UFznjm1P9jFspdlXdc9H8K3AscDyOoz5pjfFyCxwvnAJHSuqfwpe8QKq8xiNX3xyqnT4aQyVMzodXZXocmrYxWK-6SZms2w8v4vP9GvLayMtvr_7trbfFnwAAAP__EvR_pQ), according to a University of Houston [poll](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAUheHVQBfrciEhLihe4y6vnRJBuMRI2FiY2PHuRx7NDmYD39H5vx724VJO8-u_m8i0Tyx2pn3N1BpVu9LsGi01Ta4eS8m5lWVzmWaLgLcL4EWADS7lwyoejIfQC05GaA0a1f3e89H4oHwEKXoFToZrVEF4CU_ldY-gBfJkTgxQgEAQqDpHMvYKSbrnNQqlmQIKqZXatZEafdwa81E2qt2zTDybsbVlZfIfw4HhsO979x47Cm-Gw1i8PxgOvxfOIYYDryYse8o5rbdTf00u5R-s_S3BZvA7AAD__1M3b5E) released Monday. Recent polling indicated the contests were neck-and-neck. Paxton leads incumbent U.S. Sen. John Cornyn 38% to 31% in a survey of 550 likely Republican voters, with U.S. Rep. Wesley Hunt of Houston earning 17% support. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Warning: 63 banks are on the brink of collapse. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. name: Teichert in the Trenches
subject: Transcending the Super Bowl
body:
A few weeks ago, Baltimore Ravens’ coach
---
| | | | | |
---
| | **💥Transcending the Super Bowl💥******
---
|
---
🏈 I hope you all had a great Super Bowl weekend (go Seahawks!). I hadn’t intended to send a leadership lesson this week, but this example of what right looks like has been on my mind and is too good to pass up. In a world that is filled with classless leadership, this powerful, positive example should make us all stand up, take notice, and applaud! It should also rejuvenate our hope for humanity.
🦀 A few weeks ago, Baltimore Ravens’ head coach John Harbaugh was fired by owner Steve Bisciotti for shortcomings in the team’s performance. It’s what Coach Harbaugh did afterwards that is remarkable and refreshing.
🗞️ Coach Harbaugh paid for a full-page ad in the Sunday edition of _The Baltimore Sun_. In it, he expressed appreciation. He thanked his players. He thanked his coaching and support staff. He thanked the fans and the community. But it didn’t stop there.
💥 He wrote the following (to the guy who fired him): “To Steve Bisciotti: Thank you for creating an environment rooted in maintaining a standard of excellence.” No bitterness. No spite. No revenge. No doubling down by lashing out. Just grace and gratitude, class and character.
💡 That’s exactly what our society needs today as medicine to our malaise and as ointment to our acrimony: a lot more grace and gratitude, and much more class and character.
🫡 Well done Coach Harbaugh! It is an example to all of us that transcends the Super Bowl on how to LEAD WELL!

* John

| | | | **Teichert in the Trenches**

# Did you know?

Maintaining clean voter rolls is Georgia’s most vital tool for preventing voter fraud? Most importantly, accurate lists ensure that your legal vote isn't canceled out by a "ghost" record. Fraud often happens in ways you wouldn't expect: a relative might receive a mail-in ballot for a family member who passed away and decide to forge the signature, or a "double-dipper" who moved out of state might cast ballots in both jurisdictions because the old rolls weren't updated. It can even occur when ballots are sent to vacant lots or commercial buildings and intercepted by bad actors. Keeping these rolls clean isn't about exclusion—it’s about locking the door against these quiet abuses before they ever happen.

Most Mississippians assume that if our sons and daughters are sent into war, Congress has done its job--debated the issue and voted to declare it. That's what the Constitution requires. But for more than 20 years, presidents have started and expanded wars first while Congress mostly watches from the sidelines.
A Mississippi **Defend the Guard Act** would say: no more.
**What it would do:**
Mississippi's National Guard could not be deployed into _active-duty combat_ unless Congress has (1) issued a formal declaration of war, or (2) lawfully called forth the militia for the Constitution's narrow purposes--executing federal laws, repelling an invasion, or suppressing an insurrection. If Washington wants Mississippi citizen-soldiers fighting overseas, Congress must follow the Constitution it swore to uphold.
**What it would** _**not**_**do:**
It would not touch normal cooperation with federal authorities, training missions, disaster response, border or homeland security tasks under Title 32 within the United States and its territories, or other noncombat support. It would preserve the Governor's authority to consent to domestic use of the Guard under Title 32.
This is not isolationism. It's accountability.
The men and women of the Mississippi National Guard are our neighbors, coworkers, and family. They volunteer to defend this nation and do it with honor. The bare minimum we owe them is a clear, constitutional decision before they are ordered into harm's way overseas.
Since World War II, Congress hasn't issued a formal declaration of war. Yet Guard units have served in Korea, Vietnam, Iraq, Afghanistan, and elsewhere under broad "Authorizations for Use of Military Force" that get stretched across decades and continents. That's a far cry from the Founders' design that the people's representatives decide when we go to war.
A Mississippi Defend the Guard Act restores that balance. It doesn't tell Congress whether to approve any particular conflict. It simply insists that if Mississippians are to fight and bleed under federal command in combat, Congress must debate, vote, and own that decision. That's how a free republic is supposed to work.
From a liberty perspective, this matters. War is the health of big government: it justifies surveillance, debt, secret law, and emergency powers that outlive the crisis. Making undeclared, open-ended wars harder to wage also makes it harder for Washington to erode civil liberties at home--and it respects the sovereignty of our state.
* * *
## Mississippi Model -- Key Clauses to Copy
* **Deployment rule:** "No member of the Mississippi National Guard shall be released from state control into active-duty combat unless the United States Congress has (a) enacted a formal Declaration of War pursuant to Article I, Section 8, or (b) lawfully called forth the militia to execute the laws, repel an invasion, or suppress an insurrection pursuant to Article I, Section 8 and Article II."
* **Definition (active-duty combat):** "Participation in armed conflict; hazardous service in a foreign nation or foreign waters; or duties involving an instrumentality of war in a combat zone."
* **Exclusions:** "This Act does not restrict training, readiness activities, disaster relief, domestic support missions under Title 32, or noncombat support that does not meet the definition above."
* **Governor authority:** "Nothing in this Act limits the Governor's authority to consent to federal use of the Guard under Title 32 for domestic missions."
* **Construction:** "This Act shall be construed to protect constitutional war-powers requirements and the safety of Mississippi service members; it shall not impede routine federal-state cooperation."
* **Severability & effective date:** Standard clauses so one section being challenged doesn't sink the whole Act.

* * *
**What should happen next:**
Lawmakers should file and pass a Mississippi Defend the Guard Act. Citizens should demand they do so. Call your senator and representative and ask a simple question: _Will you insist that Congress follow the Constitution before sending Mississippi 's Guard into foreign combat?_

# Happy Birthday, TFVC!
---
| |
---
| Tomorrow, TFVC officially **celebrates 11 years** of hard work, sacrifice, and perseverance in defense of medical liberty and informed consent in Texas. What began as a small group of determined **“Mad Moms in Minivans”** has grown into a **powerful, statewide grassroots movement** delivering real results for Texans. Together, we’ve helped end coercive mandates, streamlined the exemption process, prohibited vaccine status discrimination, and secured over-the-counter access to ivermectin. Through persistent advocacy and engaged citizens, we’ve advanced parental rights, protected personal autonomy, and pushed back against medical tyranny. **These victories didn’t happen by accident.** They happened because ordinary Texans stood up, spoke out, and demanded better. Because of this movement, Texas is a **safer place to raise a family** and to make healthcare decisions free from pressure, coercion, or punishment. None of this would have been possible without the dedication, courage, and resolve of our supporters. **Thank you for standing with Texans for Vaccine Choice for 11 years and for helping shape the future of medical liberty in Texas!**

# **Trump called the police on Jeffrey Epstein in 2006, unsealed documents reveal**
Newly released FBI documents show **[Trump called Palm Beach police in 2006 about Epstein's alleged crimes,](https://substack.com/redirect/56fe749f-b338-4a8e-afb6-d2003a193945?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** contradicting his repeated claims he didn't know about them at the time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56fe749f-b338-4a8e-afb6-d2003a193945?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**What he said:**
* Trump told then-police chief Michael Reiter "Thank goodness you're stopping him, everyone has known he's been doing this."
* He called Ghislaine Maxwell Epstein's "operative," said "she is evil," and urged authorities to "focus on her"
* Trump claimed he "got the hell out of there" when teenagers were present around Epstein

# **Trump threatens to block US-Canada bridge opening over trade dispute**
President Donald Trump **[threatened Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/8fa315f1-e8f6-4095-baae-b09055115dab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to prevent the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, unless Canada negotiates with the U.S. on tariffs and "treats the United States with the Fairness and Respect that we deserve." Trump said "we will start negotiations, IMMEDIATELY" and suggested the U.S. should "own, perhaps, at least one half of this asset."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8fa315f1-e8f6-4095-baae-b09055115dab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** Trump accused Canada of building the bridge with "virtually no U.S. content" after former President Obama "stupidly" gave Canada a waiver to bypass the Buy American Act, which mandates federal agencies purchase U.S.-manufactured materials. He cited Ontario removing U.S. alcohol products from liquor store shelves and claimed "the Canadian Government expects me, as President of the United States, to PERMIT them to just 'take advantage of America!' What does the United States get -- Absolutely NOTHING!"
* **What Trump said:** Trump alleged Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney "wants to make a deal with China -- which will eat Canada alive" and warned that cozying up to China would risk Canada's national sport, claiming "the first thing China will do is terminate ALL Ice Hockey being played in Canada, and permanently eliminate The Stanley Cup." He vowed not to allow the bridge opening "until the United States is fully compensated for everything we have given them."

* * *
# **Trump to overturn Obama-era greenhouse gas "endangerment finding" in major deregulation**
President Donald Trump's administration is poised to **[walk back the Obama-era 2009"endangerment finding" on Wednesday,](https://substack.com/redirect/a383bfe8-81a9-41f5-96a4-6b46b80eb66c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** which identified six greenhouse gases as posing "a threat to public health and welfare" and served as the legal foundation for sweeping EPA climate regulations including fuel economy standards and power plant emission limits.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a383bfe8-81a9-41f5-96a4-6b46b80eb66c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin called the move "the largest act of deregulation in the history of the United States," with the final rule eliminating requirements to measure, report, certify and comply with federal greenhouse gas emission standards for motor vehicles. The rollback does not yet affect power plants or oil and gas facilities, but Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said "more energy drives human flourishing" and "energy abundance is the thing that we have to focus on, not regulating certain forms of energy out."
* **What 's next:** Trump is expected to hold a White House event Wednesday with Zeldin and Energy Secretary Chris Wright to announce a new initiative for the Department of War to purchase electricity from coal-powered plants. The Washington Coal Club will name Trump the "Undisputed Champion of Coal" during the event, continuing his consistent criticism of climate regulations throughout both terms, including his 2017 withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement.

Trump said "we will start negotiations, IMMEDIATELY" and suggested the U.S. should "own, perhaps, at least one half of this asset." | | ---|---|--- Why it matters: Trump accused Canada of building the bridge with "virtually no U.S. content" after former President Obama "stupidly" gave Canada a waiver to bypass the Buy American Act, which mandates federal agencies purchase U.S.-manufactured materials. He cited Ontario removing U.S. alcohol products from liquor store shelves and claimed "the Canadian Government expects me, as President of the United States, to PERMIT them to just 'take advantage of America!' What does the United States get -- Absolutely NOTHING!" What Trump said: Trump alleged Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney "wants to make a deal with China -- which will eat Canada alive" and warned that cozying up to China would risk Canada's national sport, claiming "the first thing China will do is terminate ALL Ice Hockey being played in Canada, and permanently eliminate The Stanley Cup." He vowed not to allow the bridge opening "until the United States is fully compensated for everything we have given them." Trump to overturn Obama-era greenhouse gas "endangerment finding" in major deregulation President Donald Trump's administration is poised to which identified six greenhouse gases as posing "a threat to public health and welfare" and served as the legal foundation for sweeping EPA climate regulations including fuel economy standards and power plant emission limits. | | ---|---|--- Why it matters: EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin called the move "the largest act of deregulation in the history of the United States," with the final rule eliminating requirements to measure, report, certify and comply with federal greenhouse gas emission standards for motor vehicles. The rollback does not yet affect power plants or oil and gas facilities, but Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said "more energy drives human flourishing" and "energy abundance is the thing that we have to focus on, not regulating certain forms of energy out." What 's next: Trump is expected to hold a White House event Wednesday with Zeldin and Energy Secretary Chris Wright to announce a new initiative for the Department of War to purchase electricity from coal-powered plants. The Washington Coal Club will name Trump the "Undisputed Champion of Coal" during the event, continuing his consistent criticism of climate regulations throughout both terms, including his 2017 withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/3449a586-e3a4-4982-b35a-2d9440d63a0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The AI industry, spearheaded by giants like Nvidia, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Oracle, has ballooned into a trillion-dollar spectacle, but beneath the hype lies a precarious structure built on circular accounting practices that scream "bubble." This "circular economy of AI," as detailed in a [recent analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/e7f2afed-b20a-4b05-be2a-b470fba899cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), involves a closed-loop system where investments, contracts, and revenues recycle among a select few players, artificially inflating stock valuations without corresponding real-world demand or profitability. Dollars spent by one entity boomerang back as revenue for another, creating the illusion of explosive growth while masking underlying fragilities. Critics draw stark parallels to the dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, warning that this self-reinforcing web could collapse, wiping out trillions in market value and eroding trust in the sector for years.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.7kaAysNiua-OVgo-i2xeu-VSTPaZoqOx8DA47QjlcLM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187516505)
At the epicenter is [Nvidia](https://substack.com/redirect/35883993-bc7d-4492-a825-d12bbaccc280?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the semiconductor behemoth whose market cap has soared to $5 trillion on the back of its AI GPUs. Nvidia doesn't just sell chips; it invests heavily in its customers to ensure future purchases, exemplifying circular accounting. Take its proposed $100 billion investment in OpenAI: In exchange for funding massive data centers (at least 10 gigawatts), OpenAI commits to deploying millions of Nvidia GPUs. This isn't organic sales growth--it's a premeditated loop where Nvidia's outlay returns as guaranteed revenue. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang unabashedly touts this as "one of the smartest investments we can possibly imagine," predicting OpenAI could become a "multi-trillion-dollar hyperscale company." But this optimism hinges on the circle: OpenAI's expansion drives more chip buys, boosting Nvidia's stock, which in turn funds more such deals.

The interdependencies extend to hyperscalers and startups, forming a tangled web of mutual back-scratching. OpenAI, despite hemorrhaging $11.5 billion in losses last quarter, secured a $300 billion cloud deal with Oracle for 4.5 gigawatts of capacity by 2027. [Oracle](https://substack.com/redirect/31b96a19-83a0-4e56-b734-31dda4ce9da3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), in turn, must purchase $40 billion worth of Nvidia's GB200 chips--400,000 units--to fulfill it. This announcement alone spiked Oracle's stock by 36%, adding $88 billion to founder Larry Ellison's net worth, while Nvidia's shares jumped 4%, tacking on $170 billion to its market cap in a single day.

Meanwhile, OpenAI's pivot to [AMD](https://substack.com/redirect/0e7da1fe-e840-4267-bea5-54e62fb9ed53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for 6 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs includes a warrant for 160 million AMD shares (a 10% stake), vesting as deployments roll out. AMD executives hail this as delivering "tens of billions" in revenue, but it's classic circularity: OpenAI gets discounted hardware, AMD locks in sales, and the warrant ties their fortunes together, inflating valuations through anticipated synergies rather than proven earnings.

[CoreWeave](https://substack.com/redirect/758df9f9-43a8-4816-92c9-507fd5ea15f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), another AI infrastructure player, epitomizes the loop. Nvidia holds a 5% equity stake and pre-purchased $6.3 billion in cloud services from CoreWeave as a "safety net." This guarantees CoreWeave can afford more Nvidia chips, recycling funds back to Nvidia while propping up CoreWeave's expansion. [Microsoft](https://substack.com/redirect/13af270c-ec0d-436b-8557-de58c60e39dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with its 49% stake in OpenAI from $11 billion in investments, provides Azure cloud but tolerates OpenAI's diversification to Oracle and others--yet this too feeds the circle, as OpenAI's growth necessitates more Microsoft-purchased GPUs. Even government involvement via the CHIPS Act adds a layer: The U.S. took a 9.9% stake in [Intel](https://substack.com/redirect/98546fd6-97ba-45b2-8d50-a577d7664cb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($8.9 billion) and granted $2.2 billion for domestic fabs, indirectly fueling the AI chip demand without scrutinizing the circular flows.

This circular accounting distorts financial realities, turning potential losses into paper gains. Revenues aren't from broad market adoption but from pre-committed deals among insiders, creating "instantaneous value" that evaporates if one link breaks. OpenAI's non-profit shell running a for-profit arm raises red flags about governance, while the sector's "getting fatter by eating itself" suggests unsustainable bloat. Stock prices reflect hype over fundamentals: Nvidia's valuation assumes perpetual dominance, but rivals like AMD are drawn into the same vortex, their shares buoyed by these pacts rather than independent merit.

Historically, this mirrors the dot-com era's ad-buying frenzy, where companies propped each other up with no viable products. The [Bank of England detects a "hint of dotcom bubble 2.0 in AI froth,"](https://substack.com/redirect/76c27ba3-b303-46cf-bac1-5422ae0a98fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and experts warn that intertwined balance sheets amplify systemic risk.

Unlike then, AI involves real assets like data centers, but the circularity means overcapacity could lead to a glut, crashing prices. With AI investments staving off U.S. recession, a bust could be catastrophic, setting the industry back decades. Investors chasing multi-trillion valuations ignore the fragility: When the loop unravels--due to regulatory scrutiny, demand shortfalls, or a single default--the bubble bursts, revealing the emperor's new clothes. This isn't innovation; it's a high-stakes Ponzi scheme masquerading as progress, and history suggests the fallout will be severe.

We should learn from the "[broadband bubble pop](https://substack.com/redirect/036f005d-ffff-48ba-ac62-f966a7a8695d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" when the telecommunications crash of the early 2000s, also a period of massive investment, overbuilding of infrastructure, and subsequent market collapse coincided with the broader dot-com bubble burst. This time isn't different.

Peter,
